objective: Quantify the international method-to-method spread in HRS consequence distances for the same input signatures without treating a simulation ensemble as experimental truth.

source.title: Simulation dataset for benchmarking quantitative risk analysis methodologies for hydrogen refuelling stations

access_attestation.interpretation: This is an honest post-access descriptive comparison. It is not a prospective holdout and has no pass/fail acceptance threshold.

frozen_selection.selection_rule: Use every available explosion or jet-fire export for the four common HRS equipment classes. Omitted files must be absent from the source method, not removed after viewing their values.

runtime_aligned_descriptive: log-log interpolated distance to 5 kPa overpressure
log-log interpolated distance to 5 kW/m2 thermal radiation
comparison_endpoints.interpolation_rule: Interpolate log(distance) against log(effect threshold) only between two positive direct source endpoints. Never extrapolate and never replace a direct source value.

primary_outputs: source file hashes and row counts
matched-input method envelope and max/min ratio
reporting_rule.missing_value_policy: Retain non-reached or nonnumeric cells as missing and report counts; do not impute them.
reporting_rule.outlier_policy: Retain all finite source values; no value-based exclusion is allowed.

claim_boundary: The result measures variation among seven published QRA implementations for a common idealised HRS. The ensemble is not ground truth and cannot validate physical accuracy, accident frequency, site-specific separation distances, emergency actions, the station-to-vehicle dynamic loop or SAGA effectiveness.
